## Summary

**`listTools()`** advertises the `users_get_many` tool with a strict `inputSchema`:
- `user_ids`: array of strings, `minItems: 1`, `maxItems: 5`
- `required: ['user_ids']`
- `additionalProperties: false` (per the skill's requirement)

**`callTool(name, args)`** validates and executes:

| Requirement | Handling |
|---|---|
| Unknown tools | Throws `Unknown tool: <name>` |
| Extra fields | Throws `Unexpected field: <key>` (rejects anything beyond `user_ids`) |
| Non-array `user_ids` | Throws `user_ids must be an array` |
| Empty array | Throws `user_ids must not be empty` |
| More than 5 entries | Throws `user_ids must contain at most 5 entries` |
| Non-string entries | Throws `user_ids must contain only strings` |
| Duplicate ids | Throws `Duplicate user id: <id>` |
| Missing users | Not an error — emitted as `<id>: not found` |
| Order | Results are emitted one per line in request order |

A successful lookup returns `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: "<id>: <name>\n<id>: not found" }] }`, so the batch never fails entirely on missing ids — each requested id gets exactly one line.

The existing `protocol.mjs` JSON-RPC wrapper already converts thrown errors into `{error:{code:-32602,...}}` responses, so all rejections surface correctly over the wire.
